description: A single-panel table rendered as an image (Table 1), titled "The alloying effect on the mechanical and other properties of Fe–Mn–C–Al steel". The table has three header columns — "Alloying element", "Advantages", "Disadvantages" — separated by horizontal rules, with four data rows, one per alloying element. Row 1, Al: advantage "Density reduction"; disadvantage "TWIP effect weakens" with superscript citations [19,64]. Row 2, Nb: advantage "Yield stress and hot plastic flow stress improvement"; disadvantage "TWIP effect weakens" with reference [60]. Row 3, C: advantage "Stronger twinning behavior"; disadvantage "Unpredictable shear fracture" with references [68,69]. Row 4, Mn: advantage "Better mechanical performance at cryogenic temperature"; disadvantage "Little improvement of mechanical properties at room temperature" with reference [70]. The table contains no numeric property values, units, or plot axes; its content is qualitative and each disadvantage cell carries bracketed literature citation numbers. The figure argues that each of the four alloying elements Al, Nb, C and Mn brings a distinct benefit to Fe–Mn–C–Al steel while simultaneously carrying its own drawback, most notably that Al and Nb both weaken the TWIP effect, that C causes unpredictable shear fracture, and that Mn improves cryogenic but not room-temperature performance.

subfigures.description: A three-column, four-row table listing alloying elements of Fe–Mn–C–Al steel with their Advantages and Disadvantages. Columns headed "Alloying element", "Advantages", "Disadvantages"; rows for Al, Nb, C and Mn. Disadvantage cells carry superscript literature citations [19,64], [60], [68,69] and [70] respectively.

observations.observation: The table lists four alloying elements for Fe–Mn–C–Al steel: Al, Nb, C and Mn.
Al is listed with the advantage "Density reduction" and the disadvantage "TWIP effect weakens" (cited [19,64]).
Nb is listed with the advantage "Yield stress and hot plastic flow stress improvement" and the disadvantage "TWIP effect weakens" (cited [60]).
C is listed with the advantage "Stronger twinning behavior" and the disadvantage "Unpredictable shear fracture" (cited [68,69]).
Mn is listed with the advantage "Better mechanical performance at cryogenic temperature" and the disadvantage "Little improvement of mechanical properties at room temperature" (cited [70]).
Both Al and Nb share the same stated disadvantage, weakening of the TWIP effect.
The caption states the table summarises "The alloying effect on the mechanical and other properties of Fe–Mn–C–Al steel".
The table contains no numeric property values, units or measured data — all entries are qualitative descriptions.
